title: CliCommand
description: A command's own declaration: src/main/cli/<command>/<command>.json. EVERY command is a directory, whether or not it has verbs, so gaining a first verb is adding a file beside this one rather than converting a file into a directory first. Its DIRECTORY is the command word, so the name is not a field here - and a directory cannot hold two entries of one name, which is how uniqueness stops being a check. This schema lives beside what it describes rather than under rsc/schema/, which is the data domain: the CLI declaration is this repo's own interface, not corpus data.

summary.description: The one-line description shown against the command in `corpus-yoga -h`.

explanation.description: What the command's things are, by topic (#770): what reads the same in every room. A status says how this room stands and this says what it is the state of - a section of a report, a tool, a pipeline - so the status carries no explanation of its own. A topic is one sentence, or the topics beneath it; `corpus-yoga walkthrough` shows them under the command's help.

target.description: The repo-relative file the command execs, or prints when it is a .md. Its stem is the command word (#40) - held by naming.target_stem_matches_command, exactly for an executable and uppercased for a document.

calculus.description: Space-separated corpus-calculus terms and laws this command implements, each of which rsc/CALCULUS.md must define. Empty when it implements none.

step.description: Names the pipeline this command is a corpus-wide step of, when it is one. Absent otherwise.

args.description: Arguments accepted before any subcommand - the flags that attach to the bare noun, in the order they render.

r.description: Reads (#29): repo-relative path prefixes this declaration reads - the r of the rwx triad. A row names the narrowest prefixes that cover what the code opens - two narrow rows before one wide one - since a prefix nothing under it is read by says nothing, and covers a stale literal as readily as a live one (effects.extent_covered reads rows against literals). The entry is a claim the gate may hold.

w.description: Writes (#29): repo-relative path prefixes this declaration writes - the w of the triad. effects.writers_disjoint holds that no prefix is claimed by two commands, exactly or by containment.

consumes.description: Consumes (#687): repo-relative path prefixes this declaration removes after reading - a dequeue, the fourth row of the triad. A consumed prefix is another command's to write: the room's stage, tmp/stage/input, which the captures fill and the promote verbs take from, the orphan cache subtrees the cleaner removes. effects.writers_disjoint holds w prefixes disjoint across commands; a consumes prefix overlaps a producer's w by nature and is held instead to be read by the same declaration.

x.description: Invokes (#29): canonical invocation forms this declaration executes - tools and parametrised commands, the x of the triad. Wire-class x's remain in sends until the census folds them in.

sends.description: Outward calls this declaration makes (#29), keyed by the call - so a repeat is unrepresentable and the call is a value a check can compare against what the implementation invokes. Each value lists that call's occasions, one entry each. A send has no scratch form: redirecting where the result lands does not stop the call going out, so CORPUS_YOGA_NO_SEND=1 refuses it - reads degrade to UNVERIFIED, writes refuse loudly (src/main/send.py, src/main/send.sh).
